subject: Medford Public Schools Reopening Plan Community Forum
overview: District administrators presented draft plans for the 2020-2021 school year, detailing hybrid and remote learning models, health protocols, and facility upgrades. The forum served to collect community feedback before the final plan submission to the state on August 10.

items.title: Reopening Process and Timeline
items.summary: Superintendent Marice Edouard-Vincent outlined the guiding pillars of equity, consistency, and safety and noted that impact bargaining with the teachers union is ongoing ahead of the final state submission.

items.title: Health Protocols and Symptom Tracking
items.summary: Officials announced the use of a mobile symptom-tracking app and clarified that classroom closures would be determined in collaboration with the local Board of Health based on transmission evidence.

items.title: Facilities and Ventilation Upgrades
items.summary: The district is repairing ventilation systems and plans to run HVAC units 23 hours a day with open dampers to maximize fresh air intake despite increased heating costs.

items.title: Instructional Models and Remote Scheduling
items.summary: Panelists described the high school and elementary schedules, focusing on the balance of synchronous and asynchronous time and the use of Wednesdays as a remote day for all students.

items.title: Technology and Student Support Services
items.summary: The district has ordered 2,000 Chromebooks to ensure 1-to-1 access and confirmed that IEP and 504 accommodations will be maintained in both remote and hybrid settings.

items.title: Attendance and State Requirements
items.summary: Administrators noted that the state now requires formal attendance tracking and has allowed for 10 days of front-loaded professional development at the start of the year.

items.title: Transportation and Mask Requirements
items.summary: Masks will be mandatory for all students in buildings and on buses, and the district is coordinating with the MBTA to increase bus capacity for social distancing.

items.title: Special Education Evaluations and Visitor Policy
items.summary: Special education evaluations will proceed by appointment with protective shields, while general building access for visitors and volunteers will be strictly limited.

items.title: Professional Development and Parent Resources
items.summary: The district is providing staff with coaching through 'Better Lessons' and plans to launch a 'Parent University' to help families navigate remote learning platforms.
